doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Learning about improvising with Mike Karoub
summary: His father explained written versus improvised passages, and friend Mike Karoub, steered by his band-director father, shared records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How did you get into the improvising end of things?

Well I got interested in that pretty early, because like I said I started playing when I was ten and right around the same time I was getting interested in my parents’ old records. And you know I asked my Dad about what’s going on — what is this? You know I wanted to know more about what was happening, and he’d explain to me when things were written out when things were just guys “taking a ride” as he liked to call it you know. And so I got interested in that and my friend Mike Karoub and I, like I said, we were pals and getting interested in the music at the same time. He was always like one step ahead of me, like because his father was a band director. His father would say, “Hey, you should listen to this record.” And then he’d call me up and say, “I’ve got this record, I think you might like it, it’s a guy named Louis Armstrong. It’s a little bit older than the stuff you’ve been listening to, but I think you’d like that.” And so we’d get together and we’d listen to these records, and our parents would sort of give us a little steering in the right direction as far as telling us what was going on. And it was fascinating you know.
